verified_behavior: Users configure up to 50 profile-scoped avoid terms, each at most 120 characters, from the Profile preferences UI; terms are trimmed, case-deduplicated and persisted in immutable profile versions without a schema migration.

Matching applies Unicode NFKC and casefold normalization with Unicode letter/number/mark/connector boundaries. Possessives and punctuation boundaries match; partial words and embedded identifier substrings do not.

New resumes, cover letters and reviewed application answers are checked before revision/export activation. A block identifies only the configured term and output path and does not include surrounding career or answer text.

Current avoid preferences also disable history/download access to prior conflicting revisions and block local mock-adapter use before browser launch; the application becomes REVIEW_REQUIRED and prior files/history remain intact.
Avoid preferences are not copied into generation contexts/audit payloads and do not trigger job-match rescoring; independently configured profiles enforce only their own terms.
The browser displays the safe block reason and leaves the answer export unpublished. External application submission remained OFF.
limitations: This deterministic implementation does not add AI relevance scoring or prompts. Terms are evaluated locally after deterministic document/answer composition.
Local checks use SQLite and synthetic browser/server fixtures; production PostgreSQL/Docker and hosted checks were NOT_RUN under user policy.
MJ-REQ-096, MJ-REQ-106 and MJ-REQ-111 retain their existing capability states; this reference slice does not complete or shrink the original requirement denominator.
The local Node engine mismatch and dependency advisory are recorded; dependency files were not changed.
